newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-JESUS IN FORGIVING MOOD IN MADRID.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JESUS IN FORGIVING MOOD IN MADRID.

text.p: Atletico Madrid fans already surprised at the poor showing of their team have been left incredulous by the mellowing of notoriously critical club owner, Jesus Gil.

Defeat at the hands of lowly neighbours Rayo Vallecano on Wednesday left the Spanish champions 12 points off the pace with just nine games played, with most commentators writing off their championship aspirations weeks ago.
It's a situation that would normally cost an Atletico manager his job.
But instead hire-and-fire veteran Gil has offered coach Radomir Antic a new contract, and decided to point his verbal artillery across the Spanish capital to the Santiago Bernabeu stadium.
"Predrag Mijatovic is a stain on football," said Gil, in reference to Real Madrid's Montenegrin striker, who has earned a reputation for diving in the penalty area.
"We're going to Dortmund (to play the champions' league), and Real are going to bed," was another Gil jibe at Real, who failed to qualify for European competition this season.
And it's not just Antic who is relieved at Gil's change of heart.

Referees who had been known to dread being selected for Atletico games, are now praised by Gil. "We have to support the referees," says Gil, who refused even to comment on a controversial penalty awarded against his team earlier in the season.
But Gil has joined in nationwide protests at a series of sendings-off and penalties that have favoured Spain's old firm, Real Madrid and Barcelona.

"It's the league of scandal...We're going back to times past, when games were won by decree," said Gil, referring to a long-standing belief that Real Madrid enjoyed the support of Spanish dictator Francisco Franco.

After years living in the shadow of Real, Atletico finally came good last season to take an impressive league-and-cup double. Gil said the day of the championship win was the happiest of his life and the signs are the warm glow of success will take some time to disappear.
Atletico offered Antic a new contract in the aftermath of Sunday's 3-1 defeat at Valencia as a vote of confidence.
Antic -- who recently decided against taking a job with the Yugoslavian national side -- turned Gil down, saying he would wait until the situation had improved to accept the offer.
Atletico fans hope that won't be too long.
"Atletico were a shadow of themselves," said Antic on Wednesday, "We were a caricature of a team."
Thursday's newspapers carried Antic's comments, while Gil kept what was -- for him -- an almost deafening silence.
